mindmap.title: Support Vector Machine (SVM)
mindmap.description: SVM is a supervised learning algorithm used for classification and regression. It works by finding the best boundary to separate different data classes.

children.title: Core Concepts
children.description: These are the fundamental building blocks that define how SVM works. They focus on creating the most effective separation between data points.

children.title: Hyperplane and Margin
children.description: A hyperplane is the decision boundary that separates different data classes. The margin is the distance between this boundary and the nearest points.

children.title: Support Vectors
children.description: These are the data points located closest to the decision boundary. They are critical because removing them changes the entire model.

children.title: Objective
children.description: The main goal of SVM is to maximize the margin between classes. This ensures the model is as robust as possible when classifying new data.

children.title: Types and Kernels
children.description: SVM can handle both simple straight lines and complex curved boundaries. It uses special mathematical tricks to manage different data shapes.

children.title: Linear SVM
children.description: Linear SVM is used when data can be separated by a straight line. It creates a simple decision boundary to divide the classes.

children.title: Non-Linear SVM
children.description: Non-linear SVM is used when data cannot be separated by a straight line. It relies on the kernel trick to find a solution.

children.title: Kernel Trick Types
children.description: The kernel trick transforms data into higher dimensions to make it linearly separable. Common types include RBF, Polynomial, and Sigmoid kernels.

children.title: Tuning and Parameters
children.description: These settings control how the model behaves and how it handles errors. Proper tuning is necessary to prevent the model from making mistakes.

children.title: C Parameter
children.description: The C parameter balances the margin size against the number of classification errors. A high C value aims for fewer errors but a smaller margin.

children.title: Gamma Parameter
children.description: Gamma determines how much influence a single training point has on the boundary. High gamma focuses on nearby points, while low gamma considers distant ones.

children.title: Hard vs Soft Margin
children.description: Hard margins allow no errors while soft margins allow some misclassifications. Soft margins are more flexible and are controlled by the C parameter.

children.title: Performance and Use
children.description: SVM is powerful in specific scenarios but has limitations with certain data types. It is widely used across various industries for pattern recognition.

children.title: Advantages
children.description: SVM is memory efficient and works well in high-dimensional spaces. It is also robust to overfitting when parameters are tuned correctly.

children.title: Disadvantages
children.description: The algorithm can be slow for large datasets and is sensitive to noise. It is also considered a black box because it is hard to interpret.

children.title: Real-World Applications
children.description: Common uses include image classification, face detection, and handwriting recognition. It is also effective for text classification and bioinformatics tasks.
